title: Pay
items: **W-2 or 1099?** As a 1099 contractor you usually pay both halves of Social Security and Medicare tax, and you usually get no employer health insurance, retirement match or paid leave.
**Raises:** is there a set schedule, and what is it based on?
**Extra shifts and late stays:** what does an extra shift pay, and how are hours past your scheduled shift paid?

title: Schedule and call
items: **Shifts:** how long is a shift, and how many make full-time?
**Weekends and holidays:** how are they split across the group?
**Call structure:** a week at a time, or a day here and there? Weekend days, nights or both?
**Call logistics:** in-house or from home, and is it paid separately?

title: The job itself
items: **Scope:** will you do blocks, art lines and central lines? Cardiac, peds and OB cases?
**Sites:** can they send you to other hospitals in the system?
**Your employer:** a hospital, a private group or a national company? What happens to your contract if the group is sold?

title: Benefits people forget
items: **CME allowance** and days off to use it.
**PTO and holidays:** accrued or granted, and when can you use them?
**Retirement match** and when it vests.
**Disability insurance:** is it own-occupation coverage?
**License and dues:** does the employer pay for your state license, certification renewal and AAAA dues?
**Malpractice:** claims-made or occurrence? Who pays for tail coverage?

title: The fine print
items: **Non-compete:** how far, for how long, and measured from which site? In a big system it can be the farthest one.
**Termination:** is the notice period the same for both sides? Can they let you go without cause?
**Sign-on bonus or forgivable loan:** if you leave early, is repayment prorated or the full amount?
**Auto-renewal:** does the contract renew on its own, and how short is the window to opt out?
